335383.title: Dual-acyclic orientation conjecture for positive-genus triangulations
335383.statement:
Let $G$ be a triangulation on a genus $g\geq 1$ orientable surface. An orientation of $G$ has vertex outdegree divisible by $3$ and at least $3$ when every vertex has outdegree divisible by $3$ and at least $3$; the dual orientation is obtained by orienting dual edges consistently with the primal orientation. **The dual-acyclic orientation conjecture.** $G$ admits an orientation of its edges such that every vertex has outdegree at least $3$, divisible by $3$, and such that there is no oriented non-contractible cycle in the dual orientation.

Such an orientation would generalize the cited positive-genus orientation theorem in a form suitable for preserving the genus of the associated spanning unicellular map; its existence is presented as an open higher-genus question.

336139.title: The permanent-non-singular $(0,k)$-matrix conjecture
336139.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let an **$(a,b)$-matrix** mean a square matrix $A_G(\eta)$ in which each vertex column occurs at most $a$ times and each edge column occurs at most $b$ times. Such a matrix is **permanent-non-singular** when its permanent is nonzero. **The permanent-non-singular $(0,k)$-matrix conjecture.** There is a constant $k$ such that every graph $G$ without isolated edges has a permanent-non-singular $(0,k)$-matrix. This is stated as a weaker conjecture than the preceding $(0,2)$-matrix claim, but the supplied material gives no resolution.

336449.title: Yan and Martinez–Savage's enumeration conjecture for restricted inversion sequences
336449.statement:
For each $n\geq1$, let $\operatorname{{\bf I}}_n$ be the set of inversion sequences

$$
\operatorname{{\bf I}}_n:=\{(e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_n):0\leq e_i<i\}.
$$

Let $\operatorname{{\bf I}}_n(\geq,\geq,-)$ be the subset of inversion sequences for which there do not exist $i<j<k$ such that $e_i\geq e_j\geq e_k$. Let $E_3(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $[n]$ avoiding enhanced $3$-crossings. **Yan and Martinez–Savage's conjecture.** The cardinality of $\operatorname{{\bf I}}_n(\geq,\geq,-)$ is $E_3(n)$. This conjecture proposes a connection between restricted inversion sequences and enhanced $3$-noncrossing partitions; the paper's stated purpose is to prove this enumeration, so the status of the conjecture should be checked against the paper's results.

336565.title: The 3-design conjecture for the trace-cubic design
336565.statement:
Let $q=2^m$ with $m 3$, let ${\mathcal{P}}={\mathrm{GF}}(q)$, and let

$$
{\mathcal{B}}_2=\{u\in {\mathrm{GF}}(q):{\mathrm{Tr}}(u^3-u)=1\}.
$$

**The trace-cubic 3-design conjecture.** If $m\not\equiv 0\pmod{4}$, then the pair $({\mathcal{P}},{\mathcal{B}}_2)$ is a $3$-design.

The preceding theorem establishes that this pair is a $2$-design. The conjecture was confirmed by Magma for $m\in\{3,5,6,7\}$, while the general assertion remains open.

336566.title: The odd-dimensional weight-enumerator conjecture for the design code
336566.statement:
Let $m\geq 3$ be odd. Let $\mathbb{D}=({\mathcal{P}},{\mathcal{B}}_2)$ be the $2$-design described in the paper, and let ${\mathcal{C}}_2(\mathbb{D})$ denote its binary code. **The odd-dimensional design-code conjecture.** The code ${\mathcal{C}}_2(\mathbb{D})$ has parameters

$$
[2^m,\,2m+1,\,2^{m-1}-2^{(m-1)/2}],
$$

with weight enumerator

$$
1+uz^{2^{m-1}-2^{(m-1)/2}}+vz^{2^{m-1}}+uz^{2^{m-1}+2^{(m-1)/2}}+z^{2^m},
$$

where

$$
u=2^{2m-1}-2^{m-1},\qquad v=2^{2m}+2^m-2.
$$

In addition, the dual code ${\mathcal{C}}_2(\mathbb{D})^\perp$ has parameters $[2^m,2^m-1-2m,6]$.

The conjecture was confirmed by Magma for $m\in\{3,5,7\}$; in those cases the code is optimal. If true, the code and its dual would support further $3$-designs.

336741.title: Wendland's five-list conjecture for facial unique-maximum coloring
336741.statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph. A **FUM-coloring** is a vertex coloring in which, on every face, the maximal color appearing on that face occurs at exactly one vertex. Suppose each vertex $v$ is assigned a list $L(v)$ of five integers.

**Wendland's conjecture.** If each vertex of a plane graph is assigned a list of $5$ integers, then there exists a FUM-coloring assigning each vertex a color from its list.

Wendland proved that lists of size $7$ suffice for FUM-coloring of every plane graph. Whether lists of size $5$ always suffice remains open.

337060.title: The edge-transitive 3-circulant modular-product conjecture

338345.title: Plex-existence conjecture for Latin squares
338345.statement:
For a Latin square of order $n$, a **$k$-plex** is a subset of cells in which each row, column, and symbol occurs exactly $k$ times. Let $N(t)$ denote the relevant set of positive integers used in the source.

**Plex-existence conjecture.** If $n$ is even, every Latin square of order $n$ has a $2k$-plex for each $k\in N(n/2)$. If $n$ is odd, every Latin square of order $n$ has a $k$-plex for each $k\in N(n)$.

The source states that this generalization of Ryser's conjecture is implied by Conjecture 8.5 of the cited survey and was independently given in the cited work. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

339233.title: The join-graph characterization of local antimagic chromatic number
339233.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $O_n$ be the empty graph of order $n$, and let $G\vee O_n$ denote their join. Write $\chi(G)$ for the chromatic number and $\chi_{la}(G)$ for the local antimagic chromatic number.

**Join characterization.** For $n\ge 1$,

$$
\chi_{la}(G\vee O_n)\ge\chi_{la}(G)+1
$$

if and only if

$$
\chi(G)=\chi_{la}(G).
$$

The claim concerns when joining an empty graph increases the local antimagic chromatic number by at least one. The preceding discussion reports counterexamples to an earlier general lower bound and gives sufficient conditions for this characterization, but does not establish it in full.

339234.title: The complete-join characterization of local antimagic chromatic number
339234.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $G\vee K_n$ denote their join. Write $\chi(G)$ for the chromatic number and $\chi_{la}(G)$ for the local antimagic chromatic number.

**Complete-join characterization.** For $n\ge 2$,

$$
\chi_{la}(G\vee K_n)\ge\chi_{la}(G)+n
$$

if and only if

$$
\chi_{la}(G)=\chi(G).
$$

The conjecture proposes an exact criterion for the local antimagic chromatic number to increase by at least $n$ under joining with a complete graph. The supplied text states the claim but gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

339445.title: Adjacent-swap connectivity conjecture for binary tropical matrix identities
339445.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a two-letter alphabet, let $w,v\in\Sigma^+$ with $w\neq v$, and let $n\geq 2$. Write $w\leftrightarrow v$ when $w$ and $v$ differ by one adjacent swap, and let $\sim_n$ denote equivalence in $\mathcal{UT}_n(\mathbb{T})$. **Adjacent-swap connectivity conjecture.**

$$
w\sim_n v
$$

if and only if there exists a positive integer $k$ and words $u(0),\ldots,u(k)$ such that

$$
w=u(0)\leftrightarrow u(1)\leftrightarrow\cdots\leftrightarrow u(k)=v
$$

and

$$
u(0)\sim_n u(1)\sim_n\cdots\sim_n u(k).
$$

The conjecture is asserted only for binary alphabets; the paper notes that it fails for alphabets of size greater than two, while it holds trivially for the previously known identities arising from a single adjacent swap.

339995.title: Maximal-consumer existence conjecture for partition consumption
339995.statement: Let $\lambda\vdash n$ be a partition, and say that a subgroup consumes a partition when it arises through the paper's consumption ordering. **The maximal-consumer existence conjecture.** For each partition $\lambda\vdash n$, there is a subgroup that consumes $\lambda$ and no partition greater than $\lambda$ in the consumption ordering. This is posed as a conjecture about the existence of a best-fit subgroup for each partition.

340115.title: Equivalent quasi-transversal conjecture for Latin squares
340115.statement:
Let $L$ be a Latin square. A **quasi-transversal** is a set of entries containing exactly one entry from each row and each column, with exactly one symbol repeated twice and every other symbol occurring once.

**Quasi-transversal conjecture.** Every Latin square has a quasi-transversal.

The source states that this is equivalent to the near-transversal conjecture by the preceding observation: deleting the repeated symbol from a quasi-transversal gives a near-transversal, and completing a near-transversal in the prescribed way gives a quasi-transversal. The source gives no resolution status.

340262.title: Generalized 2-colour conjecture for planar digraphs of prescribed digirth
340262.statement:
Let $D$ be a planar digraph with digirth at least $g$, where $g\geq 3$, and let $\vec{\chi}^\ast(D)$ denote its star dichromatic number. **Generalized 2-colour conjecture.**

$$
\vec{\chi}^\ast(D) \leq \frac{g-1}{g-2}.
$$

Equivalently, $D$ admits a colouring with $g-1$ colours such that every directed cycle in $D$ contains each colour at least once. The bound is supported by constructions whose star dichromatic numbers approach $(g-1)/(g-2)$, while the asserted upper bound is left unresolved in the supplied source.

340616.title: The sparse simplicial-complex index conjecture
340616.statement:
Let $\mathcal H\subset 2^{[n]}$ be a simplicial complex, and let $\mathcal H^{*2}_{\Delta}$ be its deleted join. Its $\mathbb Z_2$-index, denoted $\mathrm{ind}_{\mathbb Z_2}(\mathcal H^{*2}_{\Delta})$, is the least $d$ for which there is a $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant map from its polyhedron to $S^d$. **Sparse simplicial-complex index conjecture.** There exists a constant $c>1$ such that, whenever $\mathcal H$ has fewer than $c^k$ $k$-element sets,

$$
\mathrm{ind}_{\mathbb Z_2}(\mathcal H^{*2}_{\Delta})\leqslant 2k-3.
$$

Moreover, the stronger assertion that $\mathcal H$ is embeddable into $\mathbb R^{2k-3}$ may hold. The conjecture is presented as implying the preceding exponential-deficit conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution.

340618.title: Samotij–Sudakov's Kleitman analog for projective cubes in b\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}d
340618.statement: Let $n\geq 2$ and let $M$ be an integer. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ has size $|\mathcal{F}|=M$. A family is **centred** if there is an $i\in[n+1]$ such that $L_j\subseteq\mathcal{F}$ for $1\leq j<i$ and $L_j\cap\mathcal{F}=\emptyset$ for $i<j\leq n+1$. **Analog of Kleitman's theorem.** Among all such families, centred families minimise the number of $2$-cubes. This is the projective-cube analogue of Kleitman's theorem; the claim is trivial for $M\leq 2^{n-1}$, and the first non-trivial case $M=2^{n-1}+1$ is proved in the paper, while the general statement remains open.

341388.title: The AMRZ line-and-bridge conjecture for graphs without pendant edges
341388.statement: Let $G$ be a finite graph with no pendant edges. Let a **line** be a metric line in $G$, and let a **bridge** be an edge whose deletion disconnects $G$. **AMRZ line-and-bridge conjecture.** In all graphs with no pendant edges, except for finitely many cases, the number of lines plus the number of bridges is at least the number of vertices. This remains open; the statement allows finitely many exceptional graphs.

349834.title: Diameter formula for generalized Petersen graphs
349834.statement:
Let $GPG(n,s)$ be the generalized Petersen graph and let $C_n(1,s)$ be the circulant graph with step sizes $1$ and $s$. Let $n\geq 5$ and $2\leq s\leq \lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \rfloor$. **Diameter formula.** We have

$$
D(GPG(n,s)) = \begin{cases} D(C_n(1,s)) + 1 & \text{if } n=4p \text{ and } s=2p-1 \text{ with } p>2,\\ D(C_n(1,s)) + 2 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}
$$

This gives an exact relation between the diameters of generalized Petersen graphs and the corresponding circulant graphs; together with the preceding diameter bounds for $C_n(1,s)$, it yields explicit upper bounds for $GPG(n,s)$.

367578.title: Unique maximality conjecture for matroids avoiding dual symmetric-tensor circuits
367578.statement:
Let $n,t$ be non-negative integers with $n\geq t+1$, and define

$$
{\cal X}=\{K_{a,b}:a,b\geq 1,\ a+b=t+2\}.
$$

An ${\cal X}$-matroid on $K_n$ is a matroid in the family whose specified circuits are the complete bipartite graphs in ${\cal X}$.

**Unique maximality conjecture.** There is a unique maximal ${\cal X}$-matroid on $K_n$.

The preceding discussion says that the analogous family defined only by $K_{1,t+1}$ is not uniquely maximal when $t\geq 4$, motivating this conjecture; no resolution of the ${\cal X}$-matroid conjecture is supplied.

382445.title: Henning–Oellermann–Swart conjecture on the Steiner k-diameter and Steiner k-radius
382445.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a connected graph with order at least $k$. The Steiner $k$-diameter $Sd_k(G)$ and Steiner $k$-radius $Sr_k(G)$ are defined using Steiner distances over $k$-vertex subsets of $G$.

**Henning–Oellermann–Swart conjecture.**

$$
Sd_k(G)\leq\dfrac{2(k+1)}{2k-1}Sr_k(G).
$$

Henning, Oellermann and Swart proposed this bound; the paper states that it has been proved for $k=3$ and $k=4$, while the general case remains open.
